summary.en: In the British Invasion, most bands can be grouped as Beatles-type or Stones-type.
summary.zh: 在英伦入侵潮流中，大部分乐队可以被归为两类：Beatles类和Stones类。

body.zh:
在The Beatles来到美国，为英国艺人打开美国市场之后，紧接着有大量英国乐队涌入了美国。他们都类似于The Beatles的形象，一伙儿英国人身着西装、留着拖把头组成乐队。英伦入侵实际上也掀起了一股潮流，就像紧身衣、心情变色戒指或者呼啦圈一样。随便一个英国乐队，模仿The Beatles的所作所为就够好了，这一批乐队被称为“英伦入侵 (British Invasion)”。每个唱片公司都需要签下一个这样的乐队，这与Elvis Presley时期发生的事类似。Elvis于1956年签约大厂牌RCA，之后突然间RCA与Elvis席卷了整个市场，其他厂牌觉得也要找个类似的人，因此Decca签了Buddy Holly；Capital签了Gene Vincent等等。

此时我们发现有一大批乐队涌入美国市场，其中一些最终被遗忘了，只在我们研究英伦入侵的时候才会提及，他们在当时也有热门歌曲，但是之后却无法继续维持自己的音乐生涯。但也有另外一些成功渡过了英伦入侵时期，比如The Who、The Beatles、The Rolling Stones、Stevie Winwood、 Spencer Davis以及后来演变成Led Zeppelin的The Yardbirds。但是其他大部分乐队比如Gerry and the Pacemakers、The Dave Clark Five以及Freddie and the Dreamers，再听到他们的歌曲时，都已成为了回忆中的一部分，这些乐队的特点仅仅是统一着装和发型以及浓重的英国口音。但为了讲述得更有条理，我们试着给这些乐队归类，他们几乎都可以采用如下方式分类，当然在这节课之后我也会谈到一些乐队并不满足这样的分类，但是这些乐队大部分可以被归为Beatles类和Stones类。

对于Beatles类，他们强调歌曲本身以及声乐部分，他们的表演更为柔和，有很多和声以及唱片中呈现的专业音效；如果属于Stones类，则更强调布鲁斯的影响，主唱嗓音可能会更粗糙，音乐制作也不像Beatles类乐队们那样华美，这只是一种概括式的分类。

对于Beatles类的乐队，我们要讲讲同样来自利物浦、同样由Brian Epstein做经纪人、由George Martin做制作人的Gerry and the Pacemakers，在Beatles获得成功之后，他们就成为了Brian Epstein开始团结起来的另一伙人。

再比如The Dave Clark Five，这支乐队核心是鼓手Dave Clark，他拥有所有音乐的版权，但不知为何他决定不予授权那些音乐，来发行选集或者热门歌曲精选之类的东西。因此如果想上网找一些The Dave Clark Five的唱片真的很难，至少前些年我这么做的时候，花了很大力气才找到一些，因为Dave Clark不允许自己的音乐继续流通，具体为什么我也不知道，可能他在等待什么时机吧。不管怎样The Dave Clark Five是一个有趣的乐队，John Lennon害怕他们会超越The Beatles。在早期的时候，经常会听到谁将掩盖The Beatles的光芒呢？会是这支乐队么？会是那支乐队么？又或者是这支？没人料到The Beatles会有如今成就，因此John Lennon会担心，他所尊敬的The Dave Clark Five会超越自己，他觉得这支乐队很好，有很多不寻常的特质。

另一支Beatles类型的乐队是Herman's Hermits，由Peter Noone领军，我不知道他是不是刻意强调自己的口音，但当你听他唱《Mrs. Brown You've Got A Lovely Daughter》时，他的发音就有点刻意，一听就是英国歌手，尽管可能他的口音就是这样的，但是听起来还是有点刻意强调英伦入侵之中的英国味儿。Herman's Hermits的Peter Noone常说，大厂牌把别人都签走了，就剩下桶底这些，我们就是其中之一。实际上Herman's Hermits的唱片很不错，Peter Noone的演唱生涯也非常好，常有俱乐部或者赌场之类的演出。

另一个Beatles类的乐队是The Hollies，其核心人物是Graham Nash，他之后组建了Crosby, Stills, Nash有时后边还会加上Young。他们有一些热门曲目，《Bus Stop》就是其一。另一首歌叫做《Carrie Anne》，这首歌其实是关于Marianne Faithfull的，我们之前提到她有过一首热门歌曲《As Tears Go By》，她也曾经是Mick Jagger的女朋友。他们写了这首歌，但是没胆量直接叫它《Marianne》，因此叫做《Carrie Anne》，好像能掩盖真实含义。

最后一个要提到的Beatles类乐队就是Freddie and the Dreamers，他们真的是个很奇怪的乐队，仅仅符合英伦入侵的很少一部分条件。主唱叫做Freddie，乐队有一首歌叫做《Do the Freddie》，我猜他们是打算创造一种舞，唱《Do the Freddie》的时候他看上去就像在做开合跳（jumping jack）。当时的情况是，在The Ed Sullivan节目上，一群长得像The Beatles的人，主唱戴着类似于Buddy Holly的角质架框眼镜，唱着一首叫《Do the Freddie》的歌，做着开合跳在舞台上跑来跑去。如果说有些东西没留下什么历史印记，那可能这就属于其中之一，不过我们倒是可以看到其起源。其他诸如Chad and Jeremy和Peter and Gordon，都被认为是Beatles类乐队，他们注重人声和歌曲，音乐中没什么棱角。

与之相反，还有一种风格叫Stones类型。这些Stones类型的乐队受到布鲁斯的影响，实际上很多这种风格的成员们，在英伦入侵之后的六十年代末到七十年代之后，音乐生涯发展得都很好。最好的例子就是The Yardbirds，我们提过他们在Crawdaddy俱乐部很成功，由Giorgio Gomelsky做经纪人。乐队第一任重要的吉他手是Eric Clapton，尽管这么说不完全准确，之前我们提过他在乐队录了第一张单曲后就退出了，因为他觉得他们的音乐太倾向于流行音乐。他转而跟John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers一起工作，这给予了Eric Clapton音乐的真实性和吸引力。他走后 Jeff Beck接替其位置。吉他手Jimmy Page在乐队贝斯手退出后以贝斯手的身份加入乐队，Jimmy Page是个参与过很多录音的乐手，但他决定要加入一支乐队。之后大家觉得Jimmy Page怎么能弹贝斯呢，还是让他当吉他手吧，因此Jeff Beck和Jimmy Page就一起作为乐队吉他手了，他们实际上是哥们儿，彼此认识很多年了，但是他们之间的竞争导致无法共存，因此Jeff Beck离队，Jimmy Page则留了下来。随着别人都离队了，他成了唯一留下来的人。但是在之后的1968、1969年，还有很多演出要做，于是他又找来一些人，比如来自农村的孩子Robert Plant、他熟识的鼓手John Bonham以及另一个他录音时认识的John Paul Jones。他们组成了一只叫The New Yardbirds的乐队，之后更名为Led Zeppelin，可见The Yardbirds孕育了Led Zeppelin，这是之后摇滚史第二部分的内容了。

另一只Stones风格的乐队是The Animals，尽管他们并非伦敦布鲁斯中的一部分。他们的主唱叫做Eric Burdon，在《House of the Rising Sun》里，他们使用了电吉他和风琴。显然Bob Dylan听到了这首歌，这也是令他觉得需要在自己的音乐里多使用电吉他的原因之一。下节课我们会谈到 Bob Dylan在1965年的Newport Folk音乐节上开始使用电声乐器。

Georgie Fame and the Blue Flames，你可能很少听到他们的名字，除了他们著名的吉他手John McLaughlin，以及后来加入Jimmy Hendrix Experience乐队的Mitch Mitchell。

还有The Graham Bond Organisation，John McLaughlin也在其中呆过。这支乐队其中的两人Jack Bruce和Ginger Baker后来与Eric Clapton组建了Cream乐队。

还有The Zombies，核心成员是Rod Argent，他在70年代组成了一支叫做Simply Argent的乐队。

Zoot Money's Big Roll Band，他的吉他手Andy Summers在70年代末到80年代成为了The Police的成员。

还有The Spencer Davis Group，这支乐队里有年轻的Stevie Winwood，说他年轻是因为那时他只有十几岁，他的嗓音在包括The Rolling Stones在内的所有Stones类型的英国乐队里，听起来最像50年代末美国黑人布鲁斯歌手的声音。Spencer Davis唱片中厉害的声音，竟从一个十几岁的瘦小孩口发出，在嗓音上能与之一较高下的，可能只有Eric Burdon了。

因此当我们谈到The Beatles和The Rolling Stones的时候，我们把其他的英伦入侵乐队几乎都可以归类为Beatles类型或者Stones类型。当然我们不能拘泥于这种分类，因为有些乐队无法被归类。有这么两支乐队，无路如何努力去归类，都无法完全符合这两种类型，这就是The Kinks和The Who。我们下节课要谈谈这两支乐队。
body.en:
After the Beatles opened the American market for British artists, a flood of British bands followed. They looked like the Beatles—British guys in suits with mop-tops. The Invasion also became a fad, like girdles, mood rings, or hula hoops. Any British band copying what the Beatles did was enough; that wave is called the British Invasion. Every label needed to sign one—much as after Elvis signed to major RCA in 1956 and RCA and Elvis swept the market, other labels wanted someone similar: Decca signed Buddy Holly; Capitol signed Gene Vincent; and so on.

We see a large batch enter the U.S. market. Some are finally forgotten, mentioned only when we study the Invasion; they had hits then but could not sustain careers. Others survived the Invasion years: the Who, the Beatles, the Rolling Stones, Stevie Winwood, Spencer Davis, and the Yardbirds who later became Led Zeppelin. But most others—Gerry and the Pacemakers, the Dave Clark Five, Freddie and the Dreamers—when you hear their songs now, they are already part of memory; their traits were mainly matching clothes and hair and thick British accents. For clearer telling we try to classify them; almost all fit as follows—though after this lecture I will also name bands that do not—yet most can be called Beatles-type or Stones-type.

Beatles-type emphasize the song and the vocals; performances are softer, with lots of harmony and polished record sound. Stones-type emphasize blues influence; the lead voice may be rougher; production is less glossy than Beatles-type bands. That is only a rough sorting.

Among Beatles-type bands, take Gerry and the Pacemakers—also from Liverpool, also managed by Brian Epstein, also produced by George Martin. After the Beatles succeeded, they became another group Epstein began to gather.

Or the Dave Clark Five, centered on drummer Dave Clark, who owned all the music copyrights—but for some reason decided not to license them for anthologies or greatest-hits packages. So finding Dave Clark Five records online is hard; at least years ago when I tried it took great effort, because Dave Clark would not let the music circulate. Why, I do not know—maybe waiting for some moment. Anyway the Dave Clark Five were an interesting band; John Lennon feared they might overtake the Beatles. Early on you often heard: who will eclipse the Beatles? This band? That one? Or this? No one expected the Beatles’ later stature, so Lennon worried that the Dave Clark Five, whom he respected, might surpass him—he thought they were strong, with unusual traits.

Another Beatles-type band is Herman’s Hermits, led by Peter Noone. I do not know if he stressed his accent on purpose, but when you hear him sing “Mrs. Brown You’ve Got a Lovely Daughter,” the pronunciation sounds a bit deliberate—clearly a British singer; maybe that simply was his accent, but it still sounds like leaning into British flavor within the Invasion. Peter Noone often said the majors signed everyone else and left the bottom of the barrel—and they were among them. Actually Herman’s Hermits’ records are quite good, and Noone’s performing career has been solid—clubs, casinos, and so on.

Another Beatles-type band is the Hollies, centered on Graham Nash, who later formed Crosby, Stills & Nash—sometimes with Young. They had hits including “Bus Stop.” Another is “Carrie Anne,” actually about Marianne Faithfull—we mentioned her hit “As Tears Go By” and that she was Mick Jagger’s girlfriend. They wrote the song but dared not call it “Marianne,” so “Carrie Anne,” as if masking the meaning.

Last Beatles-type to mention: Freddie and the Dreamers—really an odd band, meeting only a few Invasion criteria. The singer Freddie; they had “Do the Freddie”—I guess they meant to invent a dance; when singing it he looked like doing jumping jacks. Picture Ed Sullivan: a bunch who looked like Beatles, lead singer in Buddy Holly–style horn-rims, singing “Do the Freddie,” running around doing jumping jacks. If some things left little historical mark, this may be one—but we can still see where it came from. Others such as Chad & Jeremy and Peter & Gordon are also counted Beatles-type: vocals and songs first, little edge in the music.

Opposite that is Stones-type. These bands took blues influence; in fact many members did well after the Invasion into the late 1960s and 1970s. Best example: the Yardbirds. We said they succeeded at the Crawdaddy under Giorgio Gomelsky. First important guitarist was Eric Clapton—not entirely accurate to put it that way; as mentioned he left after the first single because the music leaned too pop. He went to John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers, which gave him authenticity and pull. Jeff Beck took his place. Jimmy Page joined on bass after the bassist left—Page had done a lot of session work but decided to join a band. Then people thought: how can Jimmy Page play bass—make him a guitarist; so Beck and Page were both guitarists. They were actually mates who had known each other for years, but rivalry made coexistence hard; Beck left, Page stayed. As others left he became the last one standing. But in 1968–69 there were still gigs to play, so he brought in rural kid Robert Plant, drummer John Bonham whom he knew, and John Paul Jones from session work. They formed the New Yardbirds, later renamed Led Zeppelin—so the Yardbirds incubated Led Zeppelin; that belongs to Part Two of rock history.

Another Stones-style band is the Animals, though they were not part of the London blues scene. Lead singer Eric Burdon; on “House of the Rising Sun” they used electric guitar and organ. Bob Dylan clearly heard it; it is one reason he felt he needed more electric guitar in his own music. Next lecture we will talk about Dylan going electric at the 1965 Newport Folk Festival.

Georgie Fame and the Blue Flames—you may rarely hear the name except for famous guitarist John McLaughlin and Mitch Mitchell, who later joined the Jimi Hendrix Experience.

Also the Graham Bond Organisation, where John McLaughlin also spent time. Two members, Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker, later formed Cream with Eric Clapton.

Also the Zombies, centered on Rod Argent, who in the 1970s formed a band called Argent (Simply Argent in the lecture’s wording).

Zoot Money’s Big Roll Band—guitarist Andy Summers became a member of the Police from the late 1970s into the 1980s.

And the Spencer Davis Group, with young Stevie Winwood—young meaning still a teenager then. Among all Stones-type British bands including the Rolling Stones, his voice sounded most like late-1950s African American blues singers. The powerful voice on Spencer Davis records came from a skinny teenage kid; the only voice that might match is Eric Burdon’s.

So when we talk about the Beatles and the Rolling Stones, we can sort almost other Invasion bands as Beatles-type or Stones-type. Of course we must not cling to the sorting, because some bands do not fit. Two bands, no matter how hard you try, never fully match either type: the Kinks and the Who. Next lecture we discuss those two.
